items.title: PDF export replaces an existing report without warning

findings.title: PDF export overwrites a fixed file name silently; user input handled with assert
findings.explanation: export_results always writes MAR_ForaLABS.pdf in the chosen folder and overwrites any existing file without asking. Missing selections use assert, which gives poor user feedback. Segment and volume names are inserted into HTML unescaped.
findings.suggestion: Use a save dialog or confirm before overwriting. Replace asserts with user messages and html.escape the names.

findings.title: PDF export replaces an existing report without warning
findings.evidence:
if not os.path.isdir(outDir):

        pdfPath = os.path.join(outDir, "MAR_ForaLABS.pdf")
        self._save_html_to_pdf(html, pdfPath)
findings.explanation: The UI asks only for a directory, then uses the same fixed PDF filename every time. Exporting another specimen to that directory can overwrite a previous report without an overwrite confirmation; the user is not choosing the existing file itself.
findings.suggestion: Use a save-file dialog with overwrite confirmation or generate unique report filenames.

claude.reason: Measures.py:583 uses a fixed filename "MAR_ForaLABS.pdf" in the user-chosen folder, with no overwrite check. The file is a derived report in a folder the user picked, so there is no concrete path to harm. This is minor usability, not safety-blocking.

gpt.reason: ForaLABS/Measures.py:221-226 selects only a directory: `outDir = qt.QFileDialog.getExistingDirectory(None, "Choose output folder")`. Lines 581-584 then use `pdfPath = os.path.join(outDir, "MAR_ForaLABS.pdf")` and `self._save_html_to_pdf(html, pdfPath)` with no existence check. Lines 557-559 and 571-575 direct QPrinter to that path and print. Re-export into the same folder can destroy a previous report without confirmation; this concrete unintended data loss is blocking under the safety policy. The checked-in CMake packaging is broken (ForaLABS/CMakeLists.txt:2-7), so normal catalog reachability is conditional on repair; the source can also be manually loaded. No runtime test was possible.

gemini.reason: In ForaLABS/Measures.py lines 578-586, `export_results(self, outDir, include=None)` constructs `pdfPath = os.path.join(outDir, "MAR_ForaLABS.pdf")` and calls `self._save_html_to_pdf(html, pdfPath)` without checking if the file already exists or prompting the user. Also at lines 183-184, 222, 248-249, 269-270, 299-300 `assert` is used for input validation, and in `render_metrics_html` (lines 480-510) volume/segment names are interpolated into HTML for QTextDocument. However, writing a fixed report name `MAR_ForaLABS.pdf` into a user-selected export folder when the user clicks "Export Report (PDF)" is an ordinary usability/soundness issue, not a blocking safety vulnerability.

items.title: TXM conversion silently overwrites an existing NRRD

findings.title: TXM conversion silently overwrites an existing NRRD
findings.explanation: The destination is constructed from the input basename and output directory at lines 631–633; when no directory is selected it defaults to the TXM directory. Importing a TXM when a same-named NRRD already exists writes over that file without checking or asking, potentially destroying unrelated or earlier image data. This path is reachable when the source module is loaded manually or packaging is repaired.
findings.suggestion: Let users choose the output filename and explicitly confirm replacement, or generate a noncolliding filename and use an atomic write.

claude.reason: ImportTXM.py:631-642 writes <safeBase>.nrrd into outDir with no existence check. outDir is user-selected and defaults to the TXM's folder (lines 200-202). The filename is sanitized, so there is no path traversal. The file is a derived conversion of the user's own input, so overwriting is a minor usability issue, not blocking.

gpt.reason: ForaLABS/ImportTXM.py:200-202 defaults the output directory to the input directory: `outDir = os.path.dirname(txmPath)`. Lines 631-633 derive `nrrdPath = os.path.join(outDir, f"{safeBase}.nrrd")`, and lines 639-642 call `writer.SetFileName(nrrdPath)` and `writer.Execute(img)` without an overwrite check; the action calls it at line 231. An existing, potentially unrelated NRRD can be destroyed without selecting that file or consenting to replacement. This is blocking data loss. Normal packaged reachability is conditional on fixing the missing module scripts in ForaLABS/CMakeLists.txt:2-7; manual loading is another path. No runtime test was possible.

gemini.reason: In ForaLABS/ImportTXM.py lines 193-203 and 626-646, `onImport` defaults `outDir` to `os.path.dirname(txmPath)` if no output directory is specified, and `saveAndLoadNRRD` writes `nrrdPath = os.path.join(outDir, f"{safeBase}.nrrd")` via `sitk.ImageFileWriter().Execute(img)` without checking whether `<safeBase>.nrrd` already exists. While real, converting `<name>.txm` to `<name>.nrrd` in the chosen or source folder on user-initiated import is expected converter behavior / minor UX concern (lack of overwrite confirmation), not a blocking safety issue.

items.title: Thickness export reuses an image for different selected inputs

findings.title: Thickness export reuses an image for different selected inputs
findings.explanation: The cached image is reused without checking the selected segment, segmentation, voxel size, or cleaning parameters. After changing inputs or recomputing with thickness unchecked, users can export or view the previous specimen's map as if it belonged to the current selection. This is non-blocking correctness feedback.
findings.suggestion: Invalidate the cache on input or parameter changes, or key it to all relevant inputs and their modification times.

claude.reason: Measures.py:886-888 writes the cached last_thick_img without checking that the segment, segmentation or parameters match. Line 393 and line 874 set the cache from different runs. A stale map can be exported or shown (line 903) after the inputs change. This is a real soundness bug, but it is ordinary and non-blocking, and the severity is closer to minor than major.

gpt.reason: ForaLABS/Measures.py:883-888 checks only `if self.last_thick_img is not None:` and then calls `sitk.WriteImage(self.last_thick_img, outPath)`, without comparing the current inputs or settings. Lines 298-315 and 900-913 similarly reuse the cache for slice display. Lines 344 and 386-393 show the cached image is updated only when thickness is computed, so computing a different selection with thickness unchecked retains the previous image. A user may unknowingly export or view the wrong specimen's map; this is major but non-blocking correctness feedback, not a demonstrated safety harm.

gemini.reason: In ForaLABS/Measures.py lines 883-888 (`export_thickness_nrrd`) and lines 900-912 (`show_thickness_in_slices`), `self.last_thick_img` is checked (`if self.last_thick_img is not None:`) and reused directly without verifying whether `segNode`, `wallSegmentId`, `voxel_mm`, `minDiamPct`, or `removeUnref` changed since `self.last_thick_img` was cached, and `compute_metrics` (lines 387-393) does not clear `self.last_thick_img` when `need_thickness` is False. This can cause stale thickness maps from a previous specimen or parameter set to be exported or displayed.

items.title: CMake installs nonexistent ForaLABS.py and omits the real module scripts

findings.title: CMake installs nonexistent ForaLABS.py and omits the real module scripts
findings.explanation: The ForaLABS/ directory has no ForaLABS.py. The actual modules, Measures.py and ImportTXM.py, are not listed in the CMake script list. slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule will fail or produce an extension with no loadable modules. The README's installation route (additional module paths) does not apply to catalog users.
findings.suggestion: Call slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule once per module (Measures and ImportTXM) with its own NAME and SCRIPTS. Remove the ForaLABS.py references, including the slicer_add_python_unittest call. Put each module's resources in its own call.

findings.title: CMakeLists.txt references nonexistent ForaLABS.py and does not install ImportTXM.py or Measures.py
findings.explanation: `ForaLABS/CMakeLists.txt` sets `MODULE_NAME` to `ForaLABS` and lists `${MODULE_NAME}.py` (`ForaLABS.py`) in `MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS` and `slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}.py)`. However, `ForaLABS.py` does not exist in the repository; the actual scripted modules are `ImportTXM.py` and `Measures.py`, neither of which is installed by CMake. As a result, configuring/building the extension via CMake will fail to find `ForaLABS.py` and neither `ImportTXM` nor `Measures` will be packaged into the extension.
findings.suggestion: Either split `ImportTXM` and `Measures` into their own module subdirectories with their own `CMakeLists.txt`, or update `ForaLABS/CMakeLists.txt` to build and install `ImportTXM.py` and `Measures.py` (and reference an existing script in `slicer_add_python_unittest`), removing the nonexistent `ForaLABS.py`.

findings.title: CMake selects a nonexistent module and omits both actual modules
findings.explanation: The repository listing has no ForaLABS/ForaLABS.py; it has Measures.py and ImportTXM.py instead. The scripted-module macro therefore refers to a nonexistent script, and neither actual module is registered for packaging, so the extension cannot be built and delivered as intended.
findings.suggestion: Configure separate scripted modules for Measures and ImportTXM, with the correct scripts, resources, and tests, then build and install the extension.

items.title: Thickness map volume and mesh colormap are filled with a single constant mean value

findings.title: Thickness map is a constant fill, and the export can use a stale cached image
findings.explanation: The thickness volume is the mean value written into every voxel of the mask, so it is not a spatial map. The README describes a Maurer/medial-distance method, which the code does not use. export_thickness_nrrd writes the cached last_thick_img whenever it exists, even if the segment or voxel size has changed. The same applies to show_thickness_in_slices. Mesh vertices are colored from this constant volume.
findings.suggestion: Store per-vertex thickness and rasterize it, or describe the output accurately. Invalidate the cache when inputs change, and update the README.

findings.title: Thickness map volume and mesh colormap are filled with a single constant mean value
findings.evidence:
# Cria imagem de espessura para visualização (opcional)
        # Voxeliza e preenche com valor médio
        try:
            mask, spacing, origin, shape = self._voxelize_poly_solid(poly, voxel_mm=float(voxel_mm))
            mask_arr = sitk.GetArrayFromImage(mask)
            thick_vol = np.zeros_like(mask_arr, dtype=np.float32)
            thick_vol[mask_arr > 0] = stats["mean_mm"]
findings.explanation: In `_thickness_map_medial_from_poly`, after computing per-vertex ray-cast thickness values, `thick_vol` is filled uniformly with the single scalar `stats["mean_mm"]` at all non-zero mask voxels. Consequently, the exported thickness NRRD volume, the slice view overlay, and the 3D mesh colormap produced by `_paint_poly_with_thickness` (which samples `thick_img` at vertex coordinates) all contain a constant value (or 0 where rounding misses the mask) rather than a spatial thickness map.
findings.suggestion: Store the per-vertex ray-cast distances directly as a point scalar array on the `vtkPolyData` for 3D mesh coloring, and interpolate or splat local thickness values into the voxel grid if a volumetric thickness map is needed.

findings.title: Thickness maps contain only the global mean
findings.evidence:
try:
            mask, spacing, origin, shape = self._voxelize_poly_solid(poly, voxel_mm=float(voxel_mm))
            mask_arr = sitk.GetArrayFromImage(mask)
            thick_vol = np.zeros_like(mask_arr, dtype=np.float32)
            thick_vol[mask_arr > 0] = stats["mean_mm"]
findings.explanation: All occupied voxels receive the same global mean; the mesh coloring samples this image. The advertised map and exported NRRD therefore do not encode spatially varying thickness, which can mislead researchers interpreting local variation. This is non-blocking correctness feedback under the index policy.
findings.suggestion: Compute spatially assigned local thickness values, validate them against known geometries, and align the documentation with the implemented method.

items.title: Tests do not exercise the advertised calculations or import

findings.title: Placeholder tests, no sample data, no scientific-use disclaimer
findings.explanation: MeasuresTest is a placeholder and the Testing/Python CMake is commented out. The pore count is a genus-based proxy that depends on mesh quality. No validation is provided.
findings.suggestion: Add a synthetic torus or shell test and sample data, and document the limits of the pore-count proxy.

findings.title: Tests do not exercise the advertised calculations or import
findings.explanation: The Measures test only displays messages; the TXM test similarly skips when its sample path is empty. Consequently neither analytic correctness nor TXM conversion is checked by these tests. This is non-blocking feedback.
findings.suggestion: Add small synthetic meshes with known measures and a redistributable TXM fixture for conversion and metadata tests.

items.title: pip_install of olefile without user confirmation

findings.title: pip_install of olefile without user confirmation
findings.explanation: Clicking Import silently installs olefile into Slicer's shared Python. The package is small, but the user is not asked first. The test also calls ensurePackages.
findings.suggestion: Ask for confirmation with a dialog before installing, and document the dependency.

findings.title: Import action installs a package without asking
findings.explanation: On the first TXM import, if olefile cannot be imported, pip modifies Slicer's shared Python environment without a confirmation dialog. This is triggered by an explicit import action rather than startup; the UI only posts a status message.
findings.suggestion: Ask before installing and handle a declined or failed installation explicitly.

items.title: OLE file handle is not closed if reading an image stream raises an exception

findings.title: OLE file handle is not closed if reading an image stream raises an exception
findings.evidence:
self._msg(f"Reading TXM (OLE): {txmPath}", 15)
            arr, meta = self.logic.readTXM(txmPath)
            if arr is None:
                raise RuntimeError("Failed to read the .txm file")
findings.explanation: `readTXM` reads the entire `.txm` OLE image stack into memory (`vol = np.empty((int(n_imgs), int(height), int(width)), dtype=np_dtype)`) without closing `ole` if an exception occurs during slice reading (lines 488-493). Using a `with olefile.OleFileIO(txmPath) as ole:` context manager would ensure the file handle is always closed on error.
findings.suggestion: Use `with olefile.OleFileIO(txmPath) as ole:` in `readTXM` so the OLE file is guaranteed to close even if a stream is missing or corrupted.
